name: 1827 Prairie Avenue — the John W. Doane house (K01; refined by T-3172, T-1896)

grade.why: Pictured: 3 of the pictures on the Images tab show it.

documented_range.note: The 1904 target to the 1911 sheet that draws the house: the T-1841 census rules it present in 1904 (present_as_mapped), and the photograph (undated, after the house's completion in 1882) shows the same main block. Its building and loss dates are not read here.

placement.position_note: The rear north corner of the K01 main body, the draft's own origin (lot frame u 15.000, v -10.250 m from the middle of the rear lot line), through the T-1250 fit of the sheet, whose own check, 1.47 m RMS, is all that is claimed. Rotation 179.449 degrees turns the plan's u axis onto the lot's own rear-to-street line; v runs SOUTH, from the north wall toward 1829.
placement.symbolic_location: 1827 S. Prairie Avenue, parcel prairie_1827 (data/street_grid/1904.json), east side of Prairie Avenue, Prairie Avenue, 18th to 20th Street (Sanborn 1911 vol. 3 sheet 28).

footprint.note: The main block read off the 1911 sheet's trace (s28fp-1827-b1 p2) in the house's frame: its west (Prairie) front at u 24.4-24.5 (the wall behind the porch and south of the pavilion), its north wall at v 0 (the trace at v -0.1), its south wall at v 15.5 (the trace at 15.46-15.71) and its east wall at u 0. The porch, the pavilion and the rear range stand on it; the rear part's 1.2 m and 1.6 m steps out on the north and south flanks (u 0-14.6) are not built (the match record); the corner feature at the south-west corner is the corner tower (bays, T-3176).

stories.note: Two full storeys over a raised basement under a mansard, as the photograph shows on the front and the south flank; the sheet's '3B' counts the mansard storey (as it does at 1729, 1801 and 1816).

construction.note: '3B stone with brick rear' on the 1911 sheet; the photograph shows coursed ashlar on the Prairie front and the south flank alike. The brick rear is the rear range (rear_wings).

stone_front.note: RECONSTRUCTED as to the stone: the print is monochrome and shows a light ashlar with darker courses between lighter ones; Lemont limestone, K02's light Chicago stone, stands for it. Laid in smooth courses over a two-course base to the basement lights' heads. T-3194: high and low in turn, as the Doane photograph lays them, the low course half the high (on the tower's broad face, where the print is sharpest, high courses about 25-30 px, about 0.3-0.35 m, between thin ones about 10-12 px, under 0.15 m; the low course is held at Lemont's least, 0.2 m, so the ratio is 0.5 and the high one at most 0.41 m), up to the main cornice's top at 9.4 m. The course heights are read, not measured: the joints are faint on the print's front and the ratio stands on the tower's face.

principal_floor_m.note: T-3189: read through the photograph's camera (data/reference_views/doane_house_1827_prairie/chicagology_doane_exterior.json) as T-3176 re-solved it on the 1911 sheet's plan: the water table's top over the raised basement stands at y 1452 px on the front beside the pavilion, grade there at y 1556-1561, about 1.3 m over grade (T-3171 had 2.0-2.2 m through a camera that stood on an assumed corner point and set the house about a third too tall). The pavilion's reads the same (y 1455 px, 1.24 m).

storey_heights_m.note: T-3189, through the re-solved camera: the string course between the storeys at y 1128 px on the front (about 5.3 m over grade; 5.1 m on the pavilion's face), and the main cornice's top at y 790 px (about 9.4 m; 9.5 m on the pavilion), over a frieze and bed moulding at y 855 px (8.6 m) above the second storey's heads. So 4.0 and 4.1 m over the 1.3 m water table; T-3171's 5.5 and 5.1 m put the cornice at 12.6 m.

wall_thickness_front_m.note: RECONSTRUCTED: a dressed-stone front's thickness inside the contract's masonry range (0.23-0.45 m), taken at its top for a three-storey stone house; no source gives it.

wall_thickness_side_m.note: RECONSTRUCTED: as the front's; no source gives it.

service_wall_brick.note: RECONSTRUCTED: the common brick K01 lays for the sheet's brick rear range; no picture sees the rear.

street_front_trim.note: T-3194: the front's windows each carry a moulded hood over their lintel, as the Doane photograph's do: K09's cornice hood on its consoles stands for the print's hoods, which are segmental and carved on the window bay south of the pavilion (x 655-745 px, y 925-960 over the upper light and y 1170-1210 over the lower, through the re-solved camera) and stand over the lintel the full width of the light. RECONSTRUCTED as to their carving: the kit's moulded cornice hood is a level one, where the print's are segmental with carved tympana under them; the hood's place, its reach past the jambs and its stand off the face are the kit's. T-3209 (piece 1 of T-3197): the window bay south of the pavilion (v 12.05) takes the print's heads in place of K09's cornice hood (`tympana`): on the principal floor a carved segmental tympanum on a 0.12 m lintel (y about 1172-1205 px in the print), on the second a shallow segmental hood rising 0.2 m on a 0.1 m lintel, the print's dentilled band standing as the same row of small leaves.

wall_head.note: The photograph's deep moulded stone cornice, run round the front and the south flank and on round the walls it does not see.

roof_form.note: The photograph's steep slated faces over the cornice, with dormers on the front: a mansard.

roof_pitch_deg.note: RECONSTRUCTED: the deck over the curb, which no picture sees, inside K05's mansard_upper range.

eave_overhang_m.note: RECONSTRUCTED: the cornice's projection, taken at K01's ordinary value; the photograph shows a deep cornice but its depth is not measured through the camera.

mansard.note: T-3189, through the re-solved camera: the slated lower faces rise steeply from the cornice (about 9.4 m) to the curb, its crest at y 553 px over the window bay south of the pavilion (about 12.3 m), a rise of about 2.9 m; a dormer under a pediment stands on the front over that bay (x 650-770 px, its light from about 9.6 to 11.1 m, y 775-655, its peak at the curb, so it stands 0.05 m up the face rather than 0.1) and another over the porch at the north end (x 190-250 px). The pavilion's crown (T-3175), read the same way: the pavilion carried up an attic from the main eave to its own cornice at about y 588 px on its face (about 12.1 m, the main curb's height; attic_m 2.9), under a steep slated roof hipped on every side from that cornice (x 350-597 px) to a point at about y 407 px (about 15.1 m) with a turned iron finial to about y 352 px (about 0.8-1 m). Built as K05's hipped crown at 47 degrees on the sides and the street end, the nearest the kit's steep range (over 45) allows: the print's rise of about 3.0 m over a half-width of about 3.4 m reads 41 degrees, so the build's point stands about 0.7 m over the print's (open in the match record). The cornice 0.65 m past the pavilion's face and sides (the kit's least past the main cornice's 0.6 m), run 6.0 m back into the main roof so its ridge is short (the photograph sees it end on, as a point). How far it runs back, which no picture shows, is reconstructed. T-3195: the dormer over the window bay moves with that bay to the print's place (front_bays), to along_m 12.25, the nearest the crown's cornice allows (the print's centres about v 12.0). T-3209 (piece 1 of T-3197): the crown's cornice brought in to 0.2 m past the pavilion's face and sides from 0.65 (the kit now allows a crown over an attic, whose eave stands a storey over the main one, to sit inside the main cornice's 0.6 m); the print's stands about at them, and its point comes down about 0.5 m with it.

roof_covering.note: Slate on the lower faces, as the photograph's coursed grey faces read; the deck over the curb is not seen and is reconstructed as tin.

stair_tread_m.note: RECONSTRUCTED: inside the contract's stair range; no source gives the treads.

stair_landing_depth_m.note: The sheet's stone range at the front's north end, 2.7 m deep in front of the west wall (s28fp-1827-b1 p1, u 24.4-27.2), read as the porch the photograph shows there: its floor is the landing the columns stand on.

stoop_width_m.note: T-3210 (piece 2 of T-3197): the flight, read through the Doane photograph's camera, rises straight in from the street under the street face's south arch, as wide as that arch's mouth (v 2.7-4.6), not across the porch's whole width. Its cheek on the south side shows as a pale coping from x 37, y 1515 px to x 112, y 1455, under a newel pedestal at x 85-112 px, y 1407-1455; its treads stand over the cheek to the north (x 0-82 px, y 1462-1492). Of the two readings the print leaves, the camera holds only this one. A cheek running along the front (u 27.1-28) rises south from v 3.3-4.2 at 0.45 m to v 4.6-5.5 at 1.2 m, 30 degrees, and would land on the floor (1.3 m) past the porch's south face. A flight straight in under the north arch would put its south cheek (v 2.5) at u 26.3-24.9, inside the porch under its floor. Straight in, with its south cheek at v 4.6, the coping runs from u 28.4, 0.52 m to u 27.05, 1.24 m (28 degrees, the stair's 29.5): it meets the floor at the porch's street edge (u 27.1), and the newel pedestal stands on the arcade's line. The floor carried on north to the porch's north end and south to its south face as terraces at the landing's height (the door, at v 2.55, stands on the north one). The width's last 0.1 m and the cheek's coping are within tolerance of the print's.

entrance_bay.note: The door stands in the Prairie front's north bay (K01's 'south' end is v 0, the north wall, in this house's frame), under the porch the sheet draws over v 0-5.05; the photograph shows the porch's columns, arches and balcony at the front's north end, behind the street tree.

front_bays.note: Along the Prairie front from the north wall: the door's bay under the porch (v 2.55, the porch's centre) and the window bay south of the pavilion (x 665-745 px, one window a storey under a segmental hood). T-3195: that bay at v 12.05, read through the camera T-3176 re-solved (x 665-745 px on the front's plane is v 11.43-12.64), where T-3171's fit had put it at 12.9; its dormer moves with it as far as the pavilion's crown allows, to v 12.25 (the kit keeps a dormer 0.1 m clear of the crown's cornice, which stands 0.65 m past the pavilion's side; the print's dormer, x 650-770 px, centres about v 12.0). The pavilion's own lights are the K08 projection's.

side_bays.note: RECONSTRUCTED: the north flank's windows, which no picture sees; 1823 stands 3 m north of it.

north_bays.note: RECONSTRUCTED as to their places: the south flank's windows behind the corner, counted from the Prairie corner; the photograph shows windows on this flank (x 1180-1240 px) but sees it too obliquely, and behind a tree, to place them.

rear_bays.note: RECONSTRUCTED: the east wall's window beside the rear range, which no picture sees.

sash_by_storey.note: T-3189, through the re-solved camera: the front's principal-storey window beside the pavilion from about 1.6 to 4.3 m over grade (sill y 1432 px, head y 1210) and the second storey's from about 5.6 to 8.0 m (y 1105 and 910 px), each about 1.15 m wide (K01's widest sash, 1.15 m; 77 px through the camera at the front's angle, the print's 80 px with its frame).

basement_lights.note: The raised basement's barred lights under the front's windows (x 290-370 and 565-650 px). T-3189: through the re-solved camera the print's run from about grade to about 1.0 m (y 1475-1553 px beside the pavilion), under the 1.3 m water table; K02's two base courses hold the build's to 0.3-1.05 m, within about 0.2 m of them. T-3195: read off the Doane photograph through its re-solved camera: the grilled light under the window bay south of the pavilion runs x 664-749 px, y 1475-1557 (v 11.42-12.70 m on the front's plane, about 1.28 m across, from about 0.07 to 1.04 m over grade), as the pavilion's does (x 392-468, y 1471-1548: about 1.25 m, 0.08-1.03 m). chimneys.note: Two tall stone stacks with moulded caps stand over the south flank behind the corner in the photograph (x 1240-1300 px); their places along the flank are not read through the camera and are reconstructed.

rainwater.note: RECONSTRUCTED: one copper downpipe on the rear wall; none is read off the photograph.

window_kit.note: RECONSTRUCTED: two-over-two sash; the photograph shows one-over-one and two-light sash behind blinds, which the kit's pattern stands for. T-3195: the area lights barred, as the Doane photograph shows every basement light on the front (x 664-749 px under the window bay south of the pavilion, y 1475-1557): K08's bar grille in each light's reveal, four uprights and a ring under the head standing for the print's scrolled panel. The pattern is RECONSTRUCTED: the print's bars scroll out from a centre stem into an arch, which the kit's ring stands for.

entrance_kit.note: The sheet's stone range at the front's north end (u 24.4-27.2, v 0.05-5.05) is the porch the photograph shows there behind the street tree: columns carrying a balustraded balcony at the second floor, built as the door's hood on columns with a railing over it. T-3189, through the re-solved camera: the entablature's foot at y 1175 px at the porch's south side (about 4.85 m over grade), its balcony's railing over it to y 1130 (about 5.4 m), its floor on the columns' bases at about y 1422 (about 1.6 m). Built with its soffit at 4.7 m, a 0.2 m fascia, a 0.12 m cornice and a 0.45 m railing (to about 5.5 m), so the balcony stops under the second storey's sills over the door's bay, which the kit will not stand a railing in front of; the print's entablature reads about 0.2 m and its railing about 0.45-0.5 m. T-3210 (piece 2 of T-3197), through the same camera: the porch is an arcade in the front's stone (the print's spandrels and columns are the walls' pale stone), not joinery. On the street face two round arches on three columns, at v 0.35, 2.55 and 4.75: the print sees the south one whole (x 13-120 px), its crown at y about 1207 px (about 4.45 m) and the stone band over it to the entablature's foot, and the column between the two at x 0-15 px (v about 2.55, its capital's top at y about 1283, about 3.5 m); the north one is past the print's left edge and is built as its pair. On the south face one arch, from the respond on the wall (the print's column against the pavilion at x 233-253 px, about 0.3 m out) to the corner column behind the street tree, its capital at y about 1253-1283 (about 3.5-3.9 m). Built springing at 3.65 m off the capitals and rising 0.85 m, the front's two a true half round over their 1.7 m between capitals, the south one a half ellipse over its 2.0 m. RECONSTRUCTED: the north arch, the arches' mouldings (the print's archivolt is a thin line), and the consoles at the south end, which the arcade replaces.

T-3206: the run ends on a stone pier, as the photograph's does (x 1165-1200 px, through its camera at the lot's south corner), not on an iron post: the kit's 0.5 m pier, its cap plain, at s 21.95-22.45. bays.note: The sheet's shallow pavilion on the front (u 24.4-24.97, v 5.33-10.79: 5.46 m wide, 0.47 m out), carried full height with the photograph's three lights a storey (x 330-530 px: a wide centre light between two narrow ones), and on up an attic storey past the main cornice to its own crown (T-3175): the Doane photograph shows the pavilion rising through the mansard, three tall lights in its attic wall (x 357-500 px), under a steep pyramidal roof of its own (mansard.crown). And the corner tower (T-3176): the sheet's corner feature at the south-west corner is a square turned 45 degrees across the corner, its north-west face meeting the front at v 14.36, its angles at u 25.5, v 15.5 and u 24.0, v 17.1 and its south-east face meeting the flank at u 22.3 (2.27 m on a face, centred on u 23.98, v 15.55); the photograph's broad south-west face (x 857-1135 px) is about 3.2 m, 3.5 times the front's 1.15 m window beside it, and the camera re-fitted with the square's side free on the sheet's centre puts it at 3.25 m (4.4 px RMS; the sheet's own 2.27 m leaves 40-47 px). Built as K08's polygonal tower turned 45 degrees across the front's south corner (s_m 15.5, its centre 0.42 m inside the front and on the flank's plane, radius 2.298 m), its walls on the three faces outside the house: one light a storey on the north-west face and a pair on the south-west, read off the print, and a pair on the unseen south-east face, reconstructed. T-3189: its heights read through the re-solved camera on its broad face (grade at y 1576 px): the bands at the front's string course (5.3 m) and cornice (9.4 m), its wall top under the brackets at y 522 px (about 12.1 m), its cornice's top at y 448 (about 12.9 m); T-3194: the print's cornice is a row of plain corbel blocks (about eleven to the broad face, y 485-522 px, about 0.35 m deep) under a deep moulded crown (y 448-485), so the tower's wall is carried to 12.5 m, the blocks' top, and K10's moulded stone eave (0.36 m, 0.32 m out) is its crown, to about 12.86 m against the print's 12.9; T-3195: the corbel blocks are built, K08's corbel table under the crown on every face (blocks 0.16 m across at most 0.28 m apart, 0.35 m deep under the wall top and 0.2 m out, kept 0.1 m off each corner: eleven to the broad face, as the print counts), the print's stepped soffit under each block reconstructed as a plain one; a slated hip at pitch 2.52 cut to a deck about 1.0 m across at about 16.5 m (y 175 px, over the tower's centre), an iron crest 0.6 m tall round the deck (y 140-175 px, to about 17.0 m) and a turned finial on each corner (the print shows the near two, y 88-130, to about 17.6 m). T-3176 had read them in proportion to T-3171's 12.6 m cornice, which put the deck at 22.0 m. T-3194: its lights and the pavilion's stand in a moulded surround, jambs 0.12 m broad (0.08 m on the tower, whose paired lights stand 0.65 m apart) on the sill's horns under a lintel 0.3 m deep standing 0.12 m proud as the hood, for the print's carved hoods and colonnettes (x 330-530 px on the pavilion, y 1170-1215 and 925-960 over its two storeys); the carving itself is reconstructed as the kit's plain moulding. T-3196: the pavilion's and the tower's first storey (5.3 m) cut at the 1.3 m water table into a basement storey and the principal one (4.0 m, its lights' sills 0.3 m over that line where they had been 1.6 m over grade), so a band runs round both at the print's water table (y about 1458-1480 px) and each carries its grilled basement light under it, on a plinth lowered to 0.05 m. T-3209 (piece 1 of T-3197): the pavilion's lights carry the print's carved tympana on a lintel cut to 0.12 m (k08_bays.tympanum): on the principal floor one segmental arch over all three lights (4.2 m across, rising 0.45 m) with the centre light's own arch rising 0.3 m over it, the panels reading at y about 1177-1213 px against the print's 1175-1215; on the second floor an arched panel over the centre light (crown about 8.0 m, y about 925 against 922-955) and a level carved panel over each narrow light. The carving, finer than the print's pixels, is a row of lozenges and bosses standing for its foliage (L-k01-1827-doane-3171). The attic storey's outer 1.0 m on the front and its returns are slated as cheeks (`cheeks`), the print's stone face between them (x about 355-525 px, the cheek on its south side x 535-600).

what_it_supplies: The water's edge beside the Illinois Central from about 40 m north of 18th Street to about 80 m south of it, and the easternmost track on to the paper's edge, as of 1911
The 1800 Prairie lot and the Glessner House footprint (stone, courtyard plan) as of 1911, and every Prairie- and Calumet-facing footprint from 18th to 20th Street

Architecture above the footprint beyond its story count, material colour and roof symbol
The lake edge beyond the stretch the sheet actually inks: the pen line stops while the tracks run on

research_note: The John W. Doane house (1882, reported architect Theodore V. Wadskier), moved off the district draft onto K01 by T-3171 (piece 1 of T-1895) under the draft's own id: the 1911 sheet's main block in coursed stone, two storeys over a raised basement under a slated mansard with pedimented dormers, the shallow pavilion on the front, the porch at the front's north end (the sheet's stone range) and the brick rear range, read through the solved camera of the Chicagology photograph (undated, after 1882). The pavilion's pyramidal roof (T-3175) and the square tower turned across the south-west corner (T-3176) are T-3172's; T-3176 re-solved the photograph's camera on the tower. docs/RESEARCH/k01-1827-doane-3171/README.md.
called: 1827 Prairie Avenue — the John W. Doane house
